params.name: transport-use-llm-generated-message-for-outbound
params.description: Whether to use LLM-generated messages for outbound SMS. When true (default), input is processed by the assistant for a response. When false, the input text is forwarded directly as the SMS message without LLM processing. Useful for sending pre-defined messages or notifications.

tools.name: chat_create-open-aichat
tools.description: Create Chat (OpenAI Compatible). Required: input. Optional: assistant, assistantId, assistantOverrides (plus 7 more).

params.name: assistant-analysis-plan-min-messages-threshold
params.description: The minimum number of messages required to run the analysis plan. If the number of messages is less than this, analysis will be skipped. @default 2

params.name: assistant-analysis-plan-outcome-ids
params.description: This is an array of outcome UUIDs to be calculated during analysis. The outcomes will be calculated and stored in `call.analysis.outcomes`.

params.name: assistant-analysis-plan-structured-data-multi-plan
params.description: This is an array of structured data plan catalogs. Each entry includes a `key` and a `plan` for generating the structured data from the call. This outputs to `call.analysis.structuredDataMulti`.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-full-message-history-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the artifact contains the full message history, even after handoff context engineering. Defaults to false.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-logging-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the call logs are enabled. Defaults to true. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-logging-path
params.description: This is the path where the call logs will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it. Usage: - If you want to upload the call logs to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-logs`. - If you want to upload the call logs to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`. @default '/'

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-logging-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call logs when storage credentials are configured. When set to false, logs will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured. Usage: - Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store logs on Vapi's storage for this assistant. - Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for logs when available. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-pcap-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the SIP packet capture is enabled. Defaults to true. Only relevant for `phone` type calls where phone number's provider is `vapi` or `byo-phone-number`. You can find the packet capture at `call.artifact.pcapUrl` after the call is ended. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-pcap-s3-path-prefix
params.description: This is the path where the SIP packet capture will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it. Usage: - If you want to upload the packet capture to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-captures`. - If you want to upload the packet capture to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`. @default '/'

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-pcap-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for SIP packet captures when storage credentials are configured. When set to false, packet captures will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured. Usage: - Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store packet captures on Vapi's storage for this assistant. - Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for packet captures when available. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-recording-enabled
params.description: This determines whether assistant's calls are recorded. Defaults to true. Usage: - If you don't want to record the calls, set this to false. - If you want to record the calls when `assistant.hipaaEnabled` (deprecated) or `assistant.compliancePlan.hipaaEnabled` explicity set this to true and make sure to provide S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. You can find the recording at `call.artifact.recordingUrl` and `call.artifact.stereoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-recording-format
params.description: This determines the format of the recording. Defaults to `wav;l16`. @default 'wav;l16'

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-recording-path
params.description: This is the path where the recording will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it. Usage: - If you want to upload the recording to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-recordings`. - If you want to upload the recording to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`. @default '/'

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-recording-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call recordings when storage credentials are configured. When set to false, recordings will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured. Usage: - Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store recordings on Vapi's storage for this assistant. - Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for recordings when available. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-scorecard-ids
params.description: This is an array of scorecard IDs that will be evaluated based on the structured outputs extracted during the call. The scorecards will be evaluated and the results will be stored in `call.artifact.scorecards` after the call has ended.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-scorecards
params.description: This is the array of scorecards that will be evaluated based on the structured outputs extracted during the call. The scorecards will be evaluated and the results will be stored in `call.artifact.scorecards` after the call has ended.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-structured-output-ids
params.description: This is an array of structured output IDs to be calculated during the call. The outputs will be extracted and stored in `call.artifact.structuredOutputs` after the call is ended.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-structured-outputs
params.description: This is an array of transient structured outputs to be calculated during the call. The outputs will be extracted and stored in `call.artifact.structuredOutputs` after the call is ended. Use this to provide inline structured output configurations instead of referencing existing ones via structuredOutputIds.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-video-recording-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the video is recorded during the call. Defaults to false. Only relevant for `webCall` type. You can find the video recording at `call.artifact.videoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended. @default false

params.name: assistant-background-sound
params.description: This is the background sound in the call. Default for phone calls is 'office' and default for web calls is 'off'. You can also provide a custom sound by providing a URL to an audio file.

params.name: assistant-client-messages
params.description: These are the messages that will be sent to your Client SDKs. Default is conversation-update,function-call,hang,model-output,speech-update,status-update,transfer-update,transcript,tool-calls,user-interrupted,voice-input,workflow.node.started,assistant.started. You can check the shape of the messages in ClientMessage schema.

params.name: assistant-compliance-plan-hipaa-enabled
params.description: When this is enabled, logs, recordings, and transcriptions will be stored in HIPAA-compliant storage. Defaults to false. Only HIPAA-compliant providers will be available for LLM, Voice, and Transcriber respectively. This setting is only honored if the organization is on an Enterprise subscription or has purchased the HIPAA add-on.

params.name: assistant-compliance-plan-pci-enabled
params.description: When this is enabled, the user will be restricted to use PCI-compliant providers, and no logs or transcripts are stored. At the end of the call, you will receive an end-of-call-report message to store on your server. Defaults to false.

params.name: assistant-compliance-plan-recording-consent-plan
params.description: Recording consent plan

params.name: assistant-credential-ids
params.description: These are the credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.

params.name: assistant-credentials
params.description: These are dynamic credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can supplement an additional credentials using this. Dynamic credentials override existing credentials.

params.name: assistant-end-call-message
params.description: This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call. If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.

params.name: assistant-end-call-phrases
params.description: This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.

params.name: assistant-first-message
params.description: This is the first message that the assistant will say. This can also be a URL to a containerized audio file (mp3, wav, etc.). If unspecified, assistant will wait for user to speak and use the model to respond once they speak.

params.name: assistant-first-message-interruptions-enabled
params.description: First message interruptions enabled

params.name: assistant-first-message-mode
params.description: This is the mode for the first message. Default is 'assistant-speaks-first'. Use: - 'assistant-speaks-first' to have the assistant speak first. - 'assistant-waits-for-user' to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first. - 'assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message' to have the assistant speak first with a message generated by the model based on the conversation state. (`assistant.model.messages` at call start, `call.messages` at squad transfer points). @default 'assistant-speaks-first'

params.name: assistant-hooks
params.description: This is a set of actions that will be performed on certain events.

params.name: assistant-keypad-input-plan-delimiters
params.description: This is the delimiter(s) that will be used to process the input. Can be '#', '*', or an empty array.

params.name: assistant-keypad-input-plan-enabled
params.description: This keeps track of whether the user has enabled keypad input. By default, it is off. @default false

params.name: assistant-keypad-input-plan-timeout-seconds
params.description: This is the time in seconds to wait before processing the input. If the input is not received within this time, the input will be ignored. If set to 'off', the input will be processed when the user enters a delimiter or immediately if no delimiter is used. @default 2

params.name: assistant-max-duration-seconds
params.description: This is the maximum number of seconds that the call will last. When the call reaches this duration, it will be ended. @default 600 (10 minutes)

params.name: assistant-metadata
params.description: This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.

params.name: assistant-model
params.description: These are the options for the assistant's LLM.

params.name: assistant-model-output-in-messages-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the model's output is used in conversation history rather than the transcription of assistant's speech. @default false

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-control-authentication-enabled
params.description: This enables authentication on the `call.monitor.controlUrl`. If `controlAuthenticationEnabled` is `true`, the `call.monitor.controlUrl` will require an `Authorization: Bearer <vapi-public-api-key>` header. @default false

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-control-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live control. Defaults to true. Fetch `call.monitor.controlUrl` to get the live control URL. To use, send any control message via a POST request to `call.monitor.controlUrl`. Here are the types of controls supported: https://docs.vapi.ai/api-reference/messages/client-inbound-message @default true

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-listen-authentication-enabled
params.description: This enables authentication on the `call.monitor.listenUrl`. If `listenAuthenticationEnabled` is `true`, the `call.monitor.listenUrl` will require an `Authorization: Bearer <vapi-public-api-key>` header. @default false

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-listen-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live listening. Defaults to true. Fetch `call.monitor.listenUrl` to get the live listening URL. @default true

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-monitor-ids
params.description: This the set of monitor ids that are attached to the assistant. The source of truth for the monitor ids is the assistant_monitor join table. This field can be used for transient assistants and to update assistants with new monitor ids. @default []

params.name: assistant-name
params.description: This is the name of the assistant. This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.

params.name: assistant-observability-plan
params.description: This is the plan for observability of assistant's calls. Currently, only Langfuse is supported.

params.name: assistant-server-credential-id
params.description: The credential ID for server authentication

params.name: assistant-server-encrypted-paths
params.description: This is the paths to encrypt in the request body if credentialId and encryptionPlan are defined.

params.name: assistant-server-headers
params.description: These are the headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value. Note: Specifying an Authorization header here will override the authorization provided by the `credentialId` (if provided). This is an anti-pattern and should be avoided outside of edge case scenarios.

params.name: assistant-server-static-ip-addresses-enabled
params.description: If enabled, requests will originate from a static set of IPs owned and managed by Vapi. @default false

params.name: assistant-server-timeout-seconds
params.description: This is the timeout in seconds for the request. Defaults to 20 seconds. @default 20

params.name: assistant-server-url
params.description: This is where the request will be sent.

params.name: assistant-server-messages
params.description: These are the messages that will be sent to your Server URL. Default is conversation-update,end-of-call-report,function-call,hang,speech-update,status-update,tool-calls,transfer-destination-request,handoff-destination-request,user-interrupted,assistant.started. You can check the shape of the messages in ServerMessage schema.

params.name: assistant-start-speaking-plan-custom-endpointing-rules
params.description: These are the custom endpointing rules to set an endpointing timeout based on a regex on the customer's speech or the assistant's last message. Usage: - If you have yes/no questions like 'are you interested in a loan?', you can set a shorter timeout. - If you have questions where the customer may pause to look up information like 'what's my account number?', you can set a longer timeout. - If you want to wait longer while customer is enumerating a list of numbers, you can set a longer timeout. These rules have the highest precedence and will override both `smartEndpointingPlan` and `transcriptionEndpointingPlan` when a rule is matched. The rules are evaluated in order and the first one that matches will be used. Order of precedence for endpointing: 1. customEndpointingRules (if any match) 2. smartEndpointingPlan (if set) 3. transcriptionEndpointingPlan @default []

params.name: assistant-start-speaking-plan-smart-endpointing-enabled
params.description: Smart endpointing enabled

params.name: assistant-start-speaking-plan-smart-endpointing-plan
params.description: This is the plan for smart endpointing. Pick between Vapi smart endpointing, LiveKit, or custom endpointing model (or nothing). We strongly recommend using livekit endpointing when working in English. LiveKit endpointing is not supported in other languages, yet. If this is set, it will override and take precedence over `transcriptionEndpointingPlan`. This plan will still be overridden by any matching `customEndpointingRules`. If this is not set, the system will automatically use the transcriber's built-in endpointing capabilities if available.

params.name: assistant-start-speaking-plan-wait-seconds
params.description: This is how long assistant waits before speaking. Defaults to 0.4. This is the minimum it will wait but if there is latency is the pipeline, this minimum will be exceeded. This is intended as a stopgap in case the pipeline is moving too fast. Example: - If model generates tokens and voice generates bytes within 100ms, the pipeline still waits 300ms before outputting speech. Usage: - If the customer is taking long pauses, set this to a higher value. - If the assistant is accidentally jumping in too much, set this to a higher value. @default 0.4

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-acknowledgement-phrases
params.description: These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met. These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-backoff-seconds
params.description: This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted. Defaults to 1. @default 1

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-interruption-phrases
params.description: These are the phrases that will always interrupt the assistant immediately, regardless of numWords. These are typically phrases indicating disagreement or desire to stop.

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-num-words
params.description: This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking. Words like 'stop', 'actually', 'no', etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value. Words like 'okay', 'yeah', 'right' will never interrupt. When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking. Defaults to 0. @default 0

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-voice-seconds
params.description: This is the seconds customer has to speak before the assistant stops talking. This uses the VAD (Voice Activity Detection) spike to determine if the customer has started speaking. Considerations: - A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds. - A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset. This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0. Defaults to 0.2 @default 0.2

params.name: assistant-overrides-start-speaking-plan-custom-endpointing-rules
params.description: These are the custom endpointing rules to set an endpointing timeout based on a regex on the customer's speech or the assistant's last message. Usage: - If you have yes/no questions like 'are you interested in a loan?', you can set a shorter timeout. - If you have questions where the customer may pause to look up information like 'what's my account number?', you can set a longer timeout. - If you want to wait longer while customer is enumerating a list of numbers, you can set a longer timeout. These rules have the highest precedence and will override both `smartEndpointingPlan` and `transcriptionEndpointingPlan` when a rule is matched. The rules are evaluated in order and the first one that matches will be used. Order of precedence for endpointing: 1. customEndpointingRules (if any match) 2. smartEndpointingPlan (if set) 3. transcriptionEndpointingPlan @default []

params.name: assistant-overrides-start-speaking-plan-smart-endpointing-enabled
params.description: Smart endpointing enabled

params.name: assistant-overrides-start-speaking-plan-smart-endpointing-plan
params.description: This is the plan for smart endpointing. Pick between Vapi smart endpointing, LiveKit, or custom endpointing model (or nothing). We strongly recommend using livekit endpointing when working in English. LiveKit endpointing is not supported in other languages, yet. If this is set, it will override and take precedence over `transcriptionEndpointingPlan`. This plan will still be overridden by any matching `customEndpointingRules`. If this is not set, the system will automatically use the transcriber's built-in endpointing capabilities if available.

params.name: assistant-overrides-start-speaking-plan-wait-seconds
params.description: This is how long assistant waits before speaking. Defaults to 0.4. This is the minimum it will wait but if there is latency is the pipeline, this minimum will be exceeded. This is intended as a stopgap in case the pipeline is moving too fast. Example: - If model generates tokens and voice generates bytes within 100ms, the pipeline still waits 300ms before outputting speech. Usage: - If the customer is taking long pauses, set this to a higher value. - If the assistant is accidentally jumping in too much, set this to a higher value. @default 0.4

params.description: These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met. These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-backoff-seconds
params.description: This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted. Defaults to 1. @default 1

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-interruption-phrases
params.description: These are the phrases that will always interrupt the assistant immediately, regardless of numWords. These are typically phrases indicating disagreement or desire to stop.

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-num-words
params.description: This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking. Words like 'stop', 'actually', 'no', etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value. Words like 'okay', 'yeah', 'right' will never interrupt. When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking. Defaults to 0. @default 0

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-voice-seconds
params.description: This is the seconds customer has to speak before the assistant stops talking. This uses the VAD (Voice Activity Detection) spike to determine if the customer has started speaking. Considerations: - A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds. - A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset. This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0. Defaults to 0.2 @default 0.2

params.name: assistant-analysis-plan-outcome-ids
params.description: This is an array of outcome UUIDs to be calculated during analysis. The outcomes will be calculated and stored in `call.analysis.outcomes`.

params.name: assistant-analysis-plan-structured-data-multi-plan
params.description: This is an array of structured data plan catalogs. Each entry includes a `key` and a `plan` for generating the structured data from the call. This outputs to `call.analysis.structuredDataMulti`.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-full-message-history-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the artifact contains the full message history, even after handoff context engineering. Defaults to false.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-logging-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the call logs are enabled. Defaults to true. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-logging-path
params.description: This is the path where the call logs will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it. Usage: - If you want to upload the call logs to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-logs`. - If you want to upload the call logs to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`. @default '/'

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-logging-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call logs when storage credentials are configured. When set to false, logs will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured. Usage: - Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store logs on Vapi's storage for this assistant. - Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for logs when available. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-pcap-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the SIP packet capture is enabled. Defaults to true. Only relevant for `phone` type calls where phone number's provider is `vapi` or `byo-phone-number`. You can find the packet capture at `call.artifact.pcapUrl` after the call is ended. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-pcap-s3-path-prefix
params.description: This is the path where the SIP packet capture will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it. Usage: - If you want to upload the packet capture to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-captures`. - If you want to upload the packet capture to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`. @default '/'

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-pcap-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for SIP packet captures when storage credentials are configured. When set to false, packet captures will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured. Usage: - Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store packet captures on Vapi's storage for this assistant. - Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for packet captures when available. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-recording-enabled
params.description: This determines whether assistant's calls are recorded. Defaults to true. Usage: - If you don't want to record the calls, set this to false. - If you want to record the calls when `assistant.hipaaEnabled` (deprecated) or `assistant.compliancePlan.hipaaEnabled` explicity set this to true and make sure to provide S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. You can find the recording at `call.artifact.recordingUrl` and `call.artifact.stereoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-recording-format
params.description: This determines the format of the recording. Defaults to `wav;l16`. @default 'wav;l16'

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-recording-path
params.description: This is the path where the recording will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it. Usage: - If you want to upload the recording to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-recordings`. - If you want to upload the recording to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`. @default '/'

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-recording-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call recordings when storage credentials are configured. When set to false, recordings will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured. Usage: - Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store recordings on Vapi's storage for this assistant. - Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for recordings when available. @default true

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-scorecard-ids
params.description: This is an array of scorecard IDs that will be evaluated based on the structured outputs extracted during the call. The scorecards will be evaluated and the results will be stored in `call.artifact.scorecards` after the call has ended.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-scorecards
params.description: This is the array of scorecards that will be evaluated based on the structured outputs extracted during the call. The scorecards will be evaluated and the results will be stored in `call.artifact.scorecards` after the call has ended.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-structured-output-ids
params.description: This is an array of structured output IDs to be calculated during the call. The outputs will be extracted and stored in `call.artifact.structuredOutputs` after the call is ended.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-structured-outputs
params.description: This is an array of transient structured outputs to be calculated during the call. The outputs will be extracted and stored in `call.artifact.structuredOutputs` after the call is ended. Use this to provide inline structured output configurations instead of referencing existing ones via structuredOutputIds.

params.name: assistant-artifact-plan-video-recording-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the video is recorded during the call. Defaults to false. Only relevant for `webCall` type. You can find the video recording at `call.artifact.videoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended. @default false

params.name: assistant-background-sound
params.description: This is the background sound in the call. Default for phone calls is 'office' and default for web calls is 'off'. You can also provide a custom sound by providing a URL to an audio file.

params.name: assistant-client-messages
params.description: These are the messages that will be sent to your Client SDKs. Default is conversation-update,function-call,hang,model-output,speech-update,status-update,transfer-update,transcript,tool-calls,user-interrupted,voice-input,workflow.node.started,assistant.started. You can check the shape of the messages in ClientMessage schema.

params.name: assistant-compliance-plan-hipaa-enabled
params.description: When this is enabled, logs, recordings, and transcriptions will be stored in HIPAA-compliant storage. Defaults to false. Only HIPAA-compliant providers will be available for LLM, Voice, and Transcriber respectively. This setting is only honored if the organization is on an Enterprise subscription or has purchased the HIPAA add-on.

params.name: assistant-compliance-plan-pci-enabled
params.description: When this is enabled, the user will be restricted to use PCI-compliant providers, and no logs or transcripts are stored. At the end of the call, you will receive an end-of-call-report message to store on your server. Defaults to false.

params.name: assistant-compliance-plan-recording-consent-plan
params.description: Recording consent plan

params.name: assistant-credential-ids
params.description: These are the credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.

params.name: assistant-credentials
params.description: These are dynamic credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can supplement an additional credentials using this. Dynamic credentials override existing credentials.

params.name: assistant-end-call-message
params.description: This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call. If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.

params.name: assistant-end-call-phrases
params.description: This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.

params.name: assistant-first-message
params.description: This is the first message that the assistant will say. This can also be a URL to a containerized audio file (mp3, wav, etc.). If unspecified, assistant will wait for user to speak and use the model to respond once they speak.

params.name: assistant-first-message-interruptions-enabled
params.description: First message interruptions enabled

params.name: assistant-first-message-mode
params.description: This is the mode for the first message. Default is 'assistant-speaks-first'. Use: - 'assistant-speaks-first' to have the assistant speak first. - 'assistant-waits-for-user' to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first. - 'assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message' to have the assistant speak first with a message generated by the model based on the conversation state. (`assistant.model.messages` at call start, `call.messages` at squad transfer points). @default 'assistant-speaks-first'

params.name: assistant-hooks
params.description: This is a set of actions that will be performed on certain events.

params.name: assistant-keypad-input-plan-delimiters
params.description: This is the delimiter(s) that will be used to process the input. Can be '#', '*', or an empty array.

params.name: assistant-keypad-input-plan-enabled
params.description: This keeps track of whether the user has enabled keypad input. By default, it is off. @default false

params.name: assistant-keypad-input-plan-timeout-seconds
params.description: This is the time in seconds to wait before processing the input. If the input is not received within this time, the input will be ignored. If set to 'off', the input will be processed when the user enters a delimiter or immediately if no delimiter is used. @default 2

params.name: assistant-max-duration-seconds
params.description: This is the maximum number of seconds that the call will last. When the call reaches this duration, it will be ended. @default 600 (10 minutes)

params.name: assistant-metadata
params.description: This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.

params.name: assistant-model
params.description: These are the options for the assistant's LLM.

params.name: assistant-model-output-in-messages-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the model's output is used in conversation history rather than the transcription of assistant's speech. @default false

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-control-authentication-enabled
params.description: This enables authentication on the `call.monitor.controlUrl`. If `controlAuthenticationEnabled` is `true`, the `call.monitor.controlUrl` will require an `Authorization: Bearer <vapi-public-api-key>` header. @default false

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-control-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live control. Defaults to true. Fetch `call.monitor.controlUrl` to get the live control URL. To use, send any control message via a POST request to `call.monitor.controlUrl`. Here are the types of controls supported: https://docs.vapi.ai/api-reference/messages/client-inbound-message @default true

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-listen-authentication-enabled
params.description: This enables authentication on the `call.monitor.listenUrl`. If `listenAuthenticationEnabled` is `true`, the `call.monitor.listenUrl` will require an `Authorization: Bearer <vapi-public-api-key>` header. @default false

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-listen-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live listening. Defaults to true. Fetch `call.monitor.listenUrl` to get the live listening URL. @default true

params.name: assistant-monitor-plan-monitor-ids
params.description: This the set of monitor ids that are attached to the assistant. The source of truth for the monitor ids is the assistant_monitor join table. This field can be used for transient assistants and to update assistants with new monitor ids. @default []

params.name: assistant-name
params.description: This is the name of the assistant. This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.

params.name: assistant-observability-plan
params.description: This is the plan for observability of assistant's calls. Currently, only Langfuse is supported.

params.name: assistant-server-credential-id
params.description: The credential ID for server authentication

params.name: assistant-server-encrypted-paths
params.description: This is the paths to encrypt in the request body if credentialId and encryptionPlan are defined.

params.name: assistant-server-headers
params.description: These are the headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value. Note: Specifying an Authorization header here will override the authorization provided by the `credentialId` (if provided). This is an anti-pattern and should be avoided outside of edge case scenarios.

params.name: assistant-server-static-ip-addresses-enabled
params.description: If enabled, requests will originate from a static set of IPs owned and managed by Vapi. @default false

params.name: assistant-server-timeout-seconds
params.description: This is the timeout in seconds for the request. Defaults to 20 seconds. @default 20

params.name: assistant-server-url
params.description: This is where the request will be sent.

params.name: assistant-server-messages
params.description: These are the messages that will be sent to your Server URL. Default is conversation-update,end-of-call-report,function-call,hang,speech-update,status-update,tool-calls,transfer-destination-request,handoff-destination-request,user-interrupted,assistant.started. You can check the shape of the messages in ServerMessage schema.

params.name: assistant-start-speaking-plan-custom-endpointing-rules
params.description: These are the custom endpointing rules to set an endpointing timeout based on a regex on the customer's speech or the assistant's last message. Usage: - If you have yes/no questions like 'are you interested in a loan?', you can set a shorter timeout. - If you have questions where the customer may pause to look up information like 'what's my account number?', you can set a longer timeout. - If you want to wait longer while customer is enumerating a list of numbers, you can set a longer timeout. These rules have the highest precedence and will override both `smartEndpointingPlan` and `transcriptionEndpointingPlan` when a rule is matched. The rules are evaluated in order and the first one that matches will be used. Order of precedence for endpointing: 1. customEndpointingRules (if any match) 2. smartEndpointingPlan (if set) 3. transcriptionEndpointingPlan @default []

params.name: assistant-start-speaking-plan-smart-endpointing-enabled
params.description: Smart endpointing enabled

params.name: assistant-start-speaking-plan-smart-endpointing-plan
params.description: This is the plan for smart endpointing. Pick between Vapi smart endpointing, LiveKit, or custom endpointing model (or nothing). We strongly recommend using livekit endpointing when working in English. LiveKit endpointing is not supported in other languages, yet. If this is set, it will override and take precedence over `transcriptionEndpointingPlan`. This plan will still be overridden by any matching `customEndpointingRules`. If this is not set, the system will automatically use the transcriber's built-in endpointing capabilities if available.

params.name: assistant-start-speaking-plan-wait-seconds
params.description: This is how long assistant waits before speaking. Defaults to 0.4. This is the minimum it will wait but if there is latency is the pipeline, this minimum will be exceeded. This is intended as a stopgap in case the pipeline is moving too fast. Example: - If model generates tokens and voice generates bytes within 100ms, the pipeline still waits 300ms before outputting speech. Usage: - If the customer is taking long pauses, set this to a higher value. - If the assistant is accidentally jumping in too much, set this to a higher value. @default 0.4

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-acknowledgement-phrases
params.description: These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met. These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-backoff-seconds
params.description: This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted. Defaults to 1. @default 1

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-interruption-phrases
params.description: These are the phrases that will always interrupt the assistant immediately, regardless of numWords. These are typically phrases indicating disagreement or desire to stop.

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-num-words
params.description: This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking. Words like 'stop', 'actually', 'no', etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value. Words like 'okay', 'yeah', 'right' will never interrupt. When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking. Defaults to 0. @default 0

params.name: assistant-stop-speaking-plan-voice-seconds
params.description: This is the seconds customer has to speak before the assistant stops talking. This uses the VAD (Voice Activity Detection) spike to determine if the customer has started speaking. Considerations: - A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds. - A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset. This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0. Defaults to 0.2 @default 0.2

params.name: assistant-transcriber
params.description: These are the options for the assistant's transcriber.

params.name: assistant-transport-configurations
params.description: These are the configurations to be passed to the transport providers of assistant's calls, like Twilio. You can store multiple configurations for different transport providers. For a call, only the configuration matching the call transport provider is used.

params.name: assistant-voice

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-logging-path

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-logging-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call logs when storage credentials are configured. When set to false, logs will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured. Usage: - Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store logs on Vapi's storage for this assistant. - Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for logs when available. @default true

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-pcap-enabled
params.description: This determines whether the SIP packet capture is enabled. Defaults to true. Only relevant for `phone` type calls where phone number's provider is `vapi` or `byo-phone-number`. You can find the packet capture at `call.artifact.pcapUrl` after the call is ended. @default true

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-pcap-s3-path-prefix
params.description: This is the path where the SIP packet capture will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it. Usage: - If you want to upload the packet capture to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-captures`. - If you want to upload the packet capture to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`. @default '/'

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-pcap-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for SIP packet captures when storage credentials are configured. params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-recording-enabled
params.description: This determines whether assistant's calls are recorded. Defaults to true. Usage: - If you don't want to record the calls, set this to false. - If you want to record the calls when `assistant.hipaaEnabled` (deprecated) or `assistant.compliancePlan.hipaaEnabled` explicity set this to true and make sure to provide S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. You can find the recording at `call.artifact.recordingUrl` and `call.artifact.stereoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended. @default true

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-recording-format
params.description: This determines the format of the recording. Defaults to `wav;l16`. @default 'wav;l16'

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-recording-path
params.description: This is the path where the recording will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard. If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it. Usage: - If you want to upload the recording to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-recordings`. - If you want to upload the recording to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`. @default '/'

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-recording-use-custom-storage-enabled
params.description: This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call recordings when storage credentials are configured. When set to false, recordings will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured. Usage: - Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store recordings on Vapi's storage for this assistant. - Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for recordings when available. @default true

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-scorecard-ids
params.description: This is an array of scorecard IDs that will be evaluated based on the structured outputs extracted during the call. The scorecards will be evaluated and the results will be stored in `call.artifact.scorecards` after the call has ended.

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-scorecards
params.description: This is the array of scorecards that will be evaluated based on the structured outputs extracted during the call. The scorecards will be evaluated and the results will be stored in `call.artifact.scorecards` after the call has ended.

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-structured-output-ids
params.description: This is an array of structured output IDs to be calculated during the call. The outputs will be extracted and stored in `call.artifact.structuredOutputs` after the call is ended.

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-structured-outputs

Use this to provide inline structured output configurations instead of referencing existing ones via structuredOutputIds.

params.name: assistant-overrides-artifact-plan-video-recording-enabled

params.name: assistant-overrides-background-sound

params.name: assistant-overrides-client-messages
params.description: These are the messages that will be sent to your Client SDKs. params.description: When this is enabled, the user will be restricted to use PCI-compliant providers, and no logs or transcripts are stored. At the end of the call, you will receive an end-of-call-report message to store on your server. Defaults to false.

params.name: assistant-overrides-keypad-input-plan-timeout-seconds
params.description: This is the time in seconds to wait before processing the input. If the input is not received within this time, the input will be ignored. If set to 'off', the input will be processed when the user enters a delimiter or immediately if no delimiter is used. @default 2

params.name: assistant-overrides-max-duration-seconds

params.name: assistant-overrides-metadata
params.description: This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.

params.name: assistant-overrides-model

params.description: This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live control. Defaults to true. Fetch `call.monitor.controlUrl` to get the live control URL. params.name: assistant-overrides-monitor-plan-listen-authentication-enabled

You can check the shape of the messages in ServerMessage schema.

params.name: assistant-overrides-start-speaking-plan-custom-endpointing-rules
params.description: These are the custom endpointing rules to set an endpointing timeout based on a regex on the customer's speech or the assistant's last message. Usage: - If you have yes/no questions like 'are you interested in a loan?', you can set a shorter timeout. - If you have questions where the customer may pause to look up information like 'what's my account number?', you can set a longer timeout. - If you want to wait longer while customer is enumerating a list of numbers, you can set a longer timeout. These rules have the highest precedence and will override both `smartEndpointingPlan` and `transcriptionEndpointingPlan` when a rule is matched. The rules are evaluated in order and the first one that matches will be used. Order of precedence for endpointing: 1. customEndpointingRules (if any match) 2. smartEndpointingPlan (if set) 3. transcriptionEndpointingPlan @default []

params.name: assistant-overrides-start-speaking-plan-smart-endpointing-enabled
params.description: Smart endpointing enabled

params.name: assistant-overrides-start-speaking-plan-smart-endpointing-plan
params.description: This is the plan for smart endpointing. Pick between Vapi smart endpointing, LiveKit, or custom endpointing model (or nothing). We strongly recommend using livekit endpointing when working in English. LiveKit endpointing is not supported in other languages, yet. If this is set, it will override and take precedence over `transcriptionEndpointingPlan`. This plan will still be overridden by any matching `customEndpointingRules`. If this is not set, the system will automatically use the transcriber's built-in endpointing capabilities if available.

params.name: assistant-overrides-start-speaking-plan-wait-seconds
params.description: This is how long assistant waits before speaking. Defaults to 0.4. This is the minimum it will wait but if there is latency is the pipeline, this minimum will be exceeded. This is intended as a stopgap in case the pipeline is moving too fast. Example: - If model generates tokens and voice generates bytes within 100ms, the pipeline still waits 300ms before outputting speech. Usage: - If the customer is taking long pauses, set this to a higher value. - If the assistant is accidentally jumping in too much, set this to a higher value. @default 0.4

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-acknowledgement-phrases
params.description: These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met. These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-backoff-seconds
params.description: This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted. Defaults to 1. @default 1

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-interruption-phrases
params.description: These are the phrases that will always interrupt the assistant immediately, regardless of numWords. These are typically phrases indicating disagreement or desire to stop.

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-num-words
params.description: This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking. Words like 'stop', 'actually', 'no', etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value. Words like 'okay', 'yeah', 'right' will never interrupt. When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking. Defaults to 0. @default 0

params.name: assistant-overrides-stop-speaking-plan-voice-seconds

Considerations: - A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds. - A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset. This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0. Defaults to 0.2 @default 0.2

tools.name: structured-output_create
tools.description: Create Structured Output. Required: name, schema. Optional: assistantIds, compliancePlan, description (plus 4 more). Returns the new StructuredOutput.

params.name: assistantIds
params.description: These are the assistant IDs that this structured output is linked to. When linked to assistants, this structured output will be available for extraction during those assistant's calls.

params.name: compliance-plan-force-store-on-hipaa-enabled
params.description: Force storage for this output under HIPAA. Only enable if output contains no sensitive data.

params.name: description
params.description: This is the description of what the structured output extracts. Use this to provide context about what data will be extracted and how it will be used.

params.name: model
params.description: This is the model that will be used to extract the structured output. To provide your own custom system and user prompts for structured output extraction, populate the messages array with your system and user messages. You can specify liquid templating in your system and user messages. Between the system or user messages, you must reference either 'transcript' or 'messages' with the `{{}}` syntax to access the conversation history. Between the system or user messages, you must reference a variation of the structured output with the `{{}}` syntax to access the structured output definition. i.e.: `{{structuredOutput}}` `{{structuredOutput.name}}` `{{structuredOutput.description}}` `{{structuredOutput.schema}}` If model is not specified, GPT-4.1 will be used by default for extraction, utilizing default system and user prompts. If messages or required fields are not specified, the default system and user prompts will be used.

params.name: name
params.description: This is the name of the structured output.

params.name: regex
params.description: This is the regex pattern to match against the transcript. Only used when type is 'regex'. Supports both raw patterns (e.g. 'd+') and regex literal format (e.g. '/d+/gi'). Uses RE2 syntax for safety. The result depends on the schema type: - boolean: true if the pattern matches, false otherwise - string: the first match or first capture group - number/integer: the first match parsed as a number - array: all matches

params.name: schema-description
params.description: This is the description to help the model understand what it needs to output.

params.name: schema-enum
params.description: This array specifies the allowed values that can be used to restrict the output of the model.

params.name: schema-format
params.description: This is the format of the string. To pass a regex, use the `pattern` property instead. OpenAI documentation: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=chat&type-restrictions=string-restrictions

params.name: schema-items-description
params.description: This is the description to help the model understand what it needs to output.

params.name: schema-items-enum
params.description: This array specifies the allowed values that can be used to restrict the output of the model.

params.name: schema-items-format
params.description: This is the format of the string. To pass a regex, use the `pattern` property instead. OpenAI documentation: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=chat&type-restrictions=string-restrictions

params.name: schema-items-pattern
params.description: This is the pattern of the string. This is a regex that will be used to validate the data in question. To use a common format, use the `format` property instead. OpenAI documentation: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs#supported-properties

params.name: schema-items-properties
params.description: This is required if the type is 'object'. This specifies the properties of the object. This is a map of property names to JsonSchema objects.

params.name: schema-items-required
params.description: This is a list of properties that are required. This only makes sense if the type is 'object'.

params.name: schema-items-title
params.description: This is the title of the schema.

params.name: schema-items-type
params.description: This is the type of output you'd like. `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean` are the primitive types and should be obvious. `array` and `object` are more interesting and quite powerful. They allow you to define nested structures. For `array`, you can define the schema of the items in the array using the `items` property. For `object`, you can define the properties of the object using the `properties` property.

params.name: schema-pattern
params.description: This is the pattern of the string. This is a regex that will be used to validate the data in question. To use a common format, use the `format` property instead. OpenAI documentation: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs#supported-properties

params.name: schema-properties
params.description: This is required if the type is 'object'. This specifies the properties of the object. This is a map of property names to JsonSchema objects.

params.name: schema-required
params.description: This is a list of properties that are required. This only makes sense if the type is 'object'.

params.name: schema-title
